system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s claims that the package is “FINAL”, “market standard” or agreed at principal level do not establish Buyer authority. In particular, Amelia Frost has not approved either fallback position.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m** general Warranty cap. The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written approval identifying this draft; none exists. | **Reject and counter at AUD 6m** — a matching fallback figure is not authorised merely because the Seller proposed it. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only the excess recoverable. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 tipping basket, with liability from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject and restore Buyer thresholds** — Seller’s proposal materially reduces recovery through both inflated thresholds and a deductible basket. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion, with limitations applying broadly to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | 24 months for general Warranty Claims, confined to that category. An 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost’s written approval; none exists. | **Reject and counter at 24 months** — 18 months is unauthorised and the catch-all wording could shorten separate claim regimes. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same general cap and time limit for “administrative simplicity”. | Separate Fundamental/Title regime: **100% cap**, at least **six years**, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject outright** — ownership, capacity and authority risks must not be diluted by the general warranty limitations. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no adequate fraud carve-out is offered. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insert an express overriding carve-out** — this protection is mandatory under the Buyer playbook and cannot be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records. | Only matters specifically and fairly disclosed with enough detail to identify their nature, scope and reasonably apparent consequences. | **Delete deemed/general disclosure** — bulk data-room and public-record disclosure improperly transfers diligence and search risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete the blanket actual, adviser and constructive-knowledge exclusion; any knowledge formulation should use appropriately named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never qualify title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject the clause** — “discoverable” matters create an impermissibly broad constructive-knowledge bar. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | Before Completion, effective Bluefen consent plus evidence that every associated condition is satisfied, in form and substance acceptable under an objective reasonableness standard. | **Make effective consent and condition satisfaction a Completion condition** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue, so endeavours or bare delivery is insufficient. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Current payout statement, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases of all security at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. | **Reject deferred release and revise funds flow** — Buyer must not acquire the Company while Riverlark debt or security remains outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are not separately itemised; Seller calls them its matter, with on-costs unconfirmed. | Specific funds-flow line item or clear Seller funding for the AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Require quantification and Seller-funded treatment** — the liability is Completion-triggered and must not be silently left in the acquired Company. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Narrow indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; relies on DD-010 showing AUD 180,000 open, without independent payment verification or confirmatory assignment. | Broader indemnity covering payment, ownership, assignment, use, infringement and resulting loss, while preserving the SOW3 payment-and-assignment cure. | **Expand the indemnity and verify the cure evidence** — payment is only one element of the IP risk and the AUD 180,000 figure is not independently verified. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; no confirmed access, breach, notification duty or loss amount. | Preservation of logs and evidence, prompt investigation, regular written updates, access to findings, and compliance/remediation obligations, while reserving remedies. | **Add investigation and information covenants without assuming an outcome** — present evidence supports neither dismissal nor a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric claim. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals—AUD 330,000 total—characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess timing, scope, termination rights, accrual and avoidability before deciding treatment; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Keep treatment open pending refreshed diligence** — the disclosures do not establish that the renewals are ordinary-course, unavoidable, accrued or non-terminable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | General limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded; Tax and IP are said to fall within the general regime. | Separate regimes for Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants, with no hidden catch-all override. | **Redraft the limitation architecture by claim category** — global wording could unintentionally cap or time-bar specifically negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on the internal Company share register at DD-012 as evidence of 100% ownership. | Independent evidence of ownership, authority and absence of encumbrances, including appropriate corporate searches, original/certified records, transaction documents and security releases. | **Do not accept DD-012 as conclusive proof** — a supplied internal register identifies the Seller’s asserted source but is not independent verification. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller asserts Tax and IP positions are settled under the general liability regime. | Treat both regimes as open for substantive negotiation; preserve category separation and do not assume either unlimited liability or resolution. | **Mark Tax and IP as expressly open** — Seller’s unilateral “settled” assertion does not establish agreement or Buyer authority. |

**Cross-cutting diligence point:** the Disclosure Letter is fixed at **5.00 pm on 22 September 2026**. Require an updated disclosure package and refreshed evidence through signing/Completion rather than treating that historic snapshot as current.
=== END ADVICE ===
